precepts.text: And makest men as the fishes of the sea, as the creeping things, that have no ruler over them. When we were without God, with no ruler, we were like creeping things; without the laws of God we were like beasts.
precepts.point: Now the scriptures substantiate the vision Peter had. The vessel knit at the four corners is Israel, and the beasts within it are men. This is why the nations cannot handle us right now: when we speak, we can use the Bible to explain itself. When they hear it, they think it is everybody. No: God said Israel was the vessel.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The vessel also held “creeping things.” Who are the creeping things? The vision was not about animals; it was about man, so there has to be a scripture showing that the creeping thing refers to man. Habakkuk says to God: “And makest men as the fishes of the sea, as the creeping things, that have no ruler over them?”

Men made as creeping things that have no ruler over them. When we were without God, with no ruler, we were like creeping things, like insects or bugs. Without the laws of God, we were like beasts, like animals.

So every creature in Peter's sheet is a description of Israel scattered without God and without his law. The creeping things are men with no ruler over them, and God was about to bring them back under his rule.

note.label: Exodus 21: The Judgments Set Before Israel

precepts.why:
If an ox that “were wont to push with his horn in time past” killed a man or a woman after “it hath been testified to his owner, and he hath not kept him in”, the ox was stoned “and his owner also shall be put to death.” Most do not have oxen today, but the same judgment reaches the yard dogs, the pit bulls, German shepherds and rottweilers. If the dog has bitten before and it was reported to you, and it gets out again through a snapped chain or a breach in the fence and mauls or kills somebody, the scripture holds the owner responsible unto death. That is why animal control writes the ticket and warns you to keep your dogs in.

But that is not the penalty today, and Habakkuk says why: “Therefore the law is slacked, and judgment doth never go forth: for the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore wrong judgment proceedeth.” The law is slack right now. Many punishments worthy of death in the scriptures, like rape or this judgment, come out today as a fine or a slap on the hand.

note.label: Psalm 94: The God of Vengeance and Defense of His People

precepts.why:
“Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” A throne is the image of power, so shall that power have fellowship with the Most High, which frames mischief by law? Habakkuk saw the same throne: “Why dost thou shew me iniquity, and cause me to behold grievance? for spoiling and violence are before me: and there are that raise up strife and contention. Therefore the law is slacked, and judgment doth never go forth: for the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore wrong judgment proceedeth.”

Iniquity, spoiling and violence are before us. The law is slack and judgment never goes forth, and wrong judgment proceeds, so our oppressors are found not guilty. That is mischief framed by a law.

The mischief framed by law is men marrying men, women marrying women, setting the new year in the midst of winter to have us worshiping another god, and coexist meaning you can serve any gods you want. The wicked compass about the righteous, and the throne that does it has no fellowship with the Most High.

This white horse had a crown, had a bow, and went forth conquering and to conquer, and the prophet Habakkuk spoke about this very same thing. “For, lo, I raise up the Chaldeans,” The Chaldeans are the upper echelon, the elite of the ancient Cushites, but this goes beyond the Cushites: this is a metaphor, a similitude for the so-called white man, Esau, like Deuteronomy 28:46 says, the curses are a sign and a wonder upon our seed for ever, and God's words are double in meaning (Job 11:6). “that bitter and hasty nation, which shall march through the breadth of the land,” From south towards the north. “to possess the dwellingplaces that are not theirs.” Didn't the conquistadors do that? You better believe they did this thing. That is why Esau is called the daughter of Babylon.

“They are terrible and dreadful: their judgment and their dignity shall proceed of themselves.” That goes with another scripture, the pride of their heart has deceived them. “Their horses also are swifter than the leopards,” Yes, they came with horses. “and are more fierce than the evening wolves: and their horsemen shall spread themselves, and their horsemen shall come from far;” Meaning Spain. “they shall fly as the eagle that hasteth to eat.” It is letting you know their symbol: the symbol of Spain was the eagle.

“They shall come all for violence:” They didn't come for spices; God says they came for violence, to conquer the twelve tribes of Israel. That was their mission, that was their goal, and they were very successful. “their faces shall sup up as the east wind,” Because they came from the east. “and they shall gather the captivity as the sand.” That is the proof: they gathered the captivity.

“And they shall scoff at the kings,” They scoffed at all the kings they found and came across; they didn't give a damn about Montezuma, Atahualpa. “and the princes shall be a scorn unto them: they shall deride every strong hold;” Whatever stronghold we had, among the Incas and the Mayans that had many strongholds, they tore into them things. Esau came with armor and they thought these dudes were invincible, until one of them, in Puerto Rico, said let's drown one of them and see if he is a god. They held him underwater with all his armor on till the last bubble came up: he's not a god, they're not gods. They went crazy going after Esau, but even then Satan was rolling with Esau; Satan said don't worry, I got this. “for they shall heap dust, and take it.”

“Then shall his mind change, and he shall pass over, and offend, imputing this his power unto his god.” Who was the god he came with? Cesare Borgia as Jesus Christ. Look at the face: they are already doing the sign of the cross. They gave credit to their god; this is not the God of our people. Then shall his mind change: after he is done raping, robbing, pillaging and destroying, he said come to Jesus, Jesus loves you, this I know, for the Bible tells me so. The women know that damn song.
“And makest men as the fishes of the sea”. Men are the fishes. As the word rises, those men learn through you; share this word, this water, throughout the whole earth.
